title: Imaginary time evolution of a quantum system through analytic continuation from real-time quantum simulation
authors: Peng Guo, Anto Shibu, Joshua Lin, Yong Zhao
abstract: Though quantum computing naturally offers an advantage for simulations of real-time quantum systems, implementing Imaginary-Time Evolution (ITE) is comparatively more difficult. Nevertheless, quantum implementations of ITE are useful both in cases where classical implementations have associated sign problems, and also as an exact method of preparing eigenstates on quantum computers. In this work we present an algorithm to obtain ITE of a generic quantum Hamiltonian by performing analytic continuation of measured real-time correlation functions. We present simulations and demonstrations on IBM quantum hardware of 1D Fokker-Planck equations for classical diffusion process and imaginary-time evolution of integrated correlation functions in 1D quantum mechanical scattering as examples to demonstrate the effectiveness of the method.
summary: This paper presents a novel algorithm to compute the imaginary-time evolution of a quantum system by analytically continuing measurable real-time correlation functions. The method is demonstrated on several 1D models, showing it provides accurate results by relating the time evolution operator to spectral properties. It is significant because it offers a pathway to ground state calculations using only real-time quantum simulation data.
main_problem: The paper develops an algorithm to calculate the imaginary-time evolution (ITE) of a quantum system by analytically continuing measurements taken in real time.
main_result: The method successfully relates ITE to real-time correlation functions, demonstrating excellent agreement with exact solutions for several 1D models.
method: The core technique involves performing analytic continuation of contour integrals derived from the Green's function, which is applied to real-time correlation functions.
model_or_system: The method is tested on generic quantum Hamiltonians, specifically applied to 1D systems including Brownian motion, the Ornstein-Uhlenbeck process, and 1D quantum mechanical scattering.
key_observables: ITE matrix elements $\langle\psi_1|e^{-\hat{H}	au}|\psi_0angle$, transition probability distributions $P(x, 	au; x', 0)$, and integrated correlation functions.
important_parameters: Imaginary time $	au$, real-time cutoff $t_{	ext{cut}}$, and a lower bound $c$ on the ground state energy.
main_assumptions: The method requires a known lower bound on the ground state energy and relies on approximating integrals by truncating the integration domain in the complex energy plane.
figures_summary: Figures compare the calculated $\mathrm{e}^{-\hat{H}	au}$ against exact solutions for various Hamiltonians, showing convergence as the real-time cutoff $t_{	ext{cut}}$ is increased.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the theoretical framework using contour deformation in the complex energy plane, deriving the relationship between real-time and imaginary-time evolution. It then applies this method to several exactly solvable 1D models, comparing results against known solutions and discussing computational limitations.
why_interesting: This work provides a powerful, theoretically grounded technique to access imaginary-time dynamics—crucial for finding ground states or thermal properties—using only real-time measurements, which is highly relevant for quantum simulation.
